label: sec:ugb-intro
html:
There have been several generalizations of Gröbner--Shirshov basis theory, coming in one of two flavors: noncommutative theory and theories for working over special ground rings, e.g.\ Euclidean domains, PID's or UFD's. Over a field, one of the main uses of a Gröbner--Shirshov basis is to find a basis for the quotient of an algebra A by a (left or two-sided) ideal I.

A consideration of the standard examples shows that the ground field k never enters into the picture. Specifically, one does not need to invert any constants, and this leads to the notion of a unital Gröbner--Shirshov basis. We view the inability of classical Gröbner--Shirshov basis techniques to apply to these mild generalizations as an unsatisfactory state of affairs.
